title: A pocket scale designed more for jewelry; 9 weight measurements
text:
A pocket scale designed more for jewelry; 9 weight measurements. [[VIDEOID:8088e7459c5eafb1cbd100e5665e391f]] This is the type of scale I use to weigh tea leaves. This is really a jewelry scale (gemstones and precious metals) that can be used for coffee or tea or food; although it is a bit small for food.

It comes with two AAA batteries and two plastic trays that act as both covers and a tray for using the tare feature. Also included is a lousy instruction sheet that doubles as an eye test since the writing is so small.

There are nine weighing units available as listed below. Note that the instruction sheet is useless and I had to do an Internet search to understand these weights.

gn = grain (based upon the mass of a single seed of cereal)
oz - ounces
ozt - troy ounces used for buying and selling precious metals
dwt = pennyweight from denarius weight (measures unit of mass)
ct = carat (for gemstones)
lb = pound
tl = tael, a unit of weight used in east Asia approximately equal to 1.3 ounce
ml = milliliter (for liquids)
g - grams

The PCS key is apparently a counting function but I have no clue how to use it. It tries to explain that but I could not get it to work.

The accuracy of this scale is a bit off but it is still functional and within a reasonable range of difference from my other scales. The current price of this scale is not listed but most scales like this range between $10 and $15.
